title: The Lake That Held Its Breath

lines.text: A calm lake in Cameroon killed more than seventeen hundred people in a single night.
lines.caps: a calm *lake in *Cameroon | killed more than *1700 people | in a single *night.

lines.text: It was Lake Nyos, in nineteen eighty six.
Deep underwater, carbon dioxide had been building up for decades, or even centuries.
lines.caps: deep *underwater | carbon dioxide | building up for *decades.

lines.text: It seeped in from below, and the heavy bottom water kept it locked in.
lines.caps: it seeped in from *below | the heavy bottom water | kept it *locked in.

lines.text: Then something disturbed the lake, and the layers of water overturned.
lines.caps: then something *disturbed | the lake | the layers *overturned.

lines.text: A huge cloud of gas poured out, and rolled downhill into the valleys.
lines.caps: a huge cloud of *gas | poured out | and rolled *downhill.

lines.text: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air. It hugs the ground, and you cannot see it.
lines.caps: carbon dioxide | is *heavier than air | you cannot *see it.

lines.text: It reached villages more than twenty kilometres away. People, cattle, and wild animals died.
lines.caps: villages *20 kilometres away | people | cattle | and *wild animals died.

lines.text: One survivor woke around midnight, to a silent village.
lines.caps: one *survivor | woke around midnight | to a *silent village.

lines.text: What set it off? Scientists still debate it.
lines.caps: what *set it off? | scientists | still *debate it.

lines.text: A landslide, or heavy rain sinking down one side of the lake, have both been suggested.
A similar lake, Monoun, had killed people two years earlier.
lines.caps: a similar lake | *Monoun | killed people *two years earlier.

lines.text: Today, pipes draw water up from the deep, so the gas can escape slowly.
lines.caps: today | *pipes draw water up | so gas escapes *slowly.

lines.text: A quiet lake, holding its breath for centuries.
Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.

sources.title: Benchmarks: August 15, 1984 & August 21, 1986: African killer lakes erupt (EARTH Magazine)
sources.supports: night of 21 Aug 1986; more than 1,700 people died; effects up to about 26 km away; CO2 built up in deep bottom waters over decades or centuries; a landslide is 'thought to be the likely trigger'; Monoun 1984; degassing pipes installed since 2001

sources.title: Lake Nyos (San Diego State University, How Volcanoes Work)
sources.supports: 21 Aug 1986; over 1,700 people plus cattle and wildlife died; CO2 denser than air so it flowed down valleys; about 23 km affected; bottom layers overturned; rain-water trigger widely believed but little evidence for landslide/earthquake; pipes siphon deep water

illustration: All imagery is the artist's illustration: villages, people and the lake are stylised; no real victims or survivors are depicted; gas cloud shapes are schematic; the chart is not to scale.
uncertain: The trigger is debated (landslide per one source, rainwater per another, volcanic gas per a minority). Reach is given as 'more than twenty kilometres' because sources say about 23 and up to 26. Omitted because sources conflict: cloud speed (70 vs 100 km/h), Monoun death toll (37 vs 34), exact time, 'August 12' typo on one page.
story_device: Cold night palette (ink black, teal, one sickly green), NOT golden; invisible gas shown by candle flames and lanterns going out, a water-layer cross-section with bubbles, ground-level fog creeping down a valley, a map ring of reach, pipe fountain at dawn; end card must differ from ep1-3 (use a still lake surface with a single rising bubble)
